"""Formula parsing and evaluation for the sheet engine."""

import re

MAX_ROW = 999


class FormulaError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a formula cannot be parsed."""


class ErrorValue(str):
    """A spreadsheet error value; a str subclass so it equals its text."""

    __slots__ = ()


ERROR = ErrorValue("#ERROR!")
CYCLE = ErrorValue("#CYCLE!")


class Number:
    __slots__ = ("value",)

    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value


class Ref:
    __slots__ = ("name",)

    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name


class UnaryOp:
    __slots__ = ("op", "operand")

    def __init__(self, op, operand):
        self.op = op
        self.operand = operand


class BinOp:
    __slots__ = ("op", "left", "right")

    def __init__(self, op, left, right):
        self.op = op
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"\s*(?:(\d+(?:\.\d+)?|[A-Za-z]+\d+)|([()+\-*/]))")


_NAME_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z]+\d+$")


def _tokenize(source):
    tokens = []
    pos = 0
    end = len(source)
    while pos < end:
        if source[pos].isspace():
            pos += 1
            continue
        match = _TOKEN_RE.match(source, pos)
        if match is None:
            raise FormulaError(f"invalid character at position {pos}")
        value, op = match.group(1), match.group(2)
        if op is not None:
            tokens.append((op, None))
        elif value[0].isdigit():
            tokens.append(("num", value))
        elif len(value) <= 4 and _NAME_TOKEN_RE.match(value):
            tokens.append(("ref", value.upper()))
        else:
            raise FormulaError(f"reference {value.upper()} is outside the sheet")
        pos = match.end()
    return tokens


_REF_RE = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]+)(\d+)$")


def _check_ref(text):
    match = _REF_RE.match(text)
    letters, digits = match.group(1), match.group(2)
    if len(letters) > 1:
        raise FormulaError(f"reference {text} is outside the sheet")
    if len(digits) > 1 and digits[0] == "0":
        raise FormulaError(f"reference {text} has a leading zero in its row")
    row = int(digits)
    if row < 1 or row > MAX_ROW:
        raise FormulaError(f"reference {text} is outside the sheet")
    return letters + digits


class _Parser:
    def __init__(self, tokens):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self):
        if self.pos < len(self.tokens):
            return self.tokens[self.pos]
        return (None, None)

    def advance(self):
        if self.pos >= len(self.tokens):
            return (None, None)
        token = self.tokens[self.pos]
        self.pos += 1
        return token

    def parse(self):
        if not self.tokens:
            raise FormulaError("empty formula")
        node = self.parse_expr()
        if self.pos != len(self.tokens):
            raise FormulaError("unexpected trailing input")
        return node

    def parse_expr(self):
        node = self.parse_term()
        while self.peek()[0] in ("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance()[0]
            node = BinOp(op, node, self.parse_term())
        return node

    def parse_term(self):
        node = self.parse_unary()
        while self.peek()[0] in ("*", "/"):
            op = self.advance()[0]
            node = BinOp(op, node, self.parse_unary())
        return node

    def parse_unary(self):
        kind = self.peek()[0]
        if kind in ("+", "-"):
            op = self.advance()[0]
            return UnaryOp(op, self.parse_unary())
        return self.parse_atom()

    def parse_atom(self):
        kind, value = self.advance()
        if kind == "num":
            return Number(int(value) if "." not in value else float(value))
        if kind == "ref":
            return Ref(_check_ref(value))
        if kind == "(":
            node = self.parse_expr()
            if self.peek()[0] != ")":
                raise FormulaError("missing closing parenthesis")
            self.advance()
            return node
        if kind == ")":
            raise FormulaError("missing opening parenthesis")
        raise FormulaError("unexpected end of formula")


def parse_formula(source: str):
    """Parse the text after the leading '=' into a syntax tree."""
    if not isinstance(source, str):
        raise FormulaError("formula source must be a string")
    return _Parser(_tokenize(source)).parse()


def references(tree) -> set:
    """Return the upper-case names of the cells a formula tree refers to."""
    names = set()
    stack = [tree]
    while stack:
        node = stack.pop()
        if isinstance(node, Ref):
            names.add(node.name)
        elif isinstance(node, BinOp):
            stack.append(node.left)
            stack.append(node.right)
        elif isinstance(node, UnaryOp):
            stack.append(node.operand)
    return names


def _to_number(value):
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return None
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, float):
        return float(value)
    return None


def _apply(op, left, right):
    if op == "+":
        return left + right
    if op == "-":
        return left - right
    if op == "*":
        return left * right
    if right == 0:
        return ERROR
    return left / right


def evaluate(tree, lookup):
    """Compute the value of a formula tree using lookup(name) for cell values."""
    if isinstance(tree, Number):
        return tree.value
    if isinstance(tree, Ref):
        value = lookup(tree.name)
        return 0 if value is None else value
    if isinstance(tree, UnaryOp):
        value = evaluate(tree.operand, lookup)
        if isinstance(value, ErrorValue):
            return value
        number = _to_number(value)
        if number is None:
            return ERROR
        if tree.op == "-":
            number = -number
        return number
    if isinstance(tree, BinOp):
        left = evaluate(tree.left, lookup)
        right = evaluate(tree.right, lookup)
        if isinstance(left, ErrorValue):
            return left
        if isinstance(right, ErrorValue):
            return right
        left_number = _to_number(left)
        right_number = _to_number(right)
        if left_number is None or right_number is None:
            return ERROR
        return _apply(tree.op, left_number, right_number)
    raise FormulaError("unknown node in formula tree")

"""Tracks which cells depend on which."""


class DependencyGraph:
    """A directed graph of formula dependencies between cells.

    A cell's precedents are the cells its formula refers to; its dependents
    are the cells whose formulas refer to it. All names are upper case.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self._pre = {}
        self._post = {}

    def set_dependencies(self, cell, precedents):
        """Replace cell's precedents with the given iterable of names."""
        new = set(precedents)
        old = self._pre.get(cell, set())
        if new != old:
            for dep in old - new:
                dependents = self._post.get(dep)
                if dependents is not None:
                    dependents.discard(cell)
                    if not dependents:
                        del self._post[dep]
            for dep in new - old:
                self._post.setdefault(dep, set()).add(cell)
        if new:
            self._pre[cell] = new
        else:
            self._pre.pop(cell, None)
            self._post.pop(cell, None)

    def precedents(self, cell) -> set:
        """Direct cells that cell's formula refers to."""
        return set(self._pre.get(cell, ()))

    def dependents(self, cell) -> set:
        """Direct cells whose formulas refer to cell."""
        return set(self._post.get(cell, ()))

    def all_dependents(self, cell) -> set:
        """Every cell that reaches cell through direct or indirect links."""
        result = set()
        stack = [cell]
        while stack:
            current = stack.pop()
            for dependent in self._post.get(current, ()):
                if dependent not in result:
                    result.add(dependent)
                    stack.append(dependent)
        return result

    def cycle_cells(self) -> set:
        """Every cell that lies on a cycle (its precedents lead back to it)."""
        nodes = set(self._pre) | set(self._post)
        on_cycle = set()
        for node in nodes:
            if node in on_cycle:
                continue
            seen = set()
            stack = list(self._pre.get(node, ()))
            found = False
            while stack:
                current = stack.pop()
                if current == node:
                    found = True
                    break
                if current in seen or current in on_cycle:
                    continue
                seen.add(current)
                stack.extend(self._pre.get(current, ()))
            if found:
                on_cycle.add(node)
        return on_cycle

"""The spreadsheet itself."""

import re

from .formula import CYCLE, evaluate, parse_formula, references
from .graph import DependencyGraph

_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^([A-Z])([1-9][0-9]{0,2})$")
_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"^-?(?:\d+)(?:\.\d+)?$")


def _sort_key(name):
    return (int(name[1:]), name[0])


def _validate(name):
    if not isinstance(name, str):
        raise ValueError(f"{name!r} is not a valid cell name")
    match = _NAME_RE.match(name.upper())
    if match is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{name!r} is outside the sheet")
    return match.group(1) + match.group(2)


class Sheet:
    """A spreadsheet with formulas, dependencies and incremental recalculation."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._raws = {}
        self._values = {}
        self._trees = {}
        self._graph = DependencyGraph()
        self.evaluations = 0

    def set(self, name: str, raw: str):
        """Store a cell's input; return the cells whose value may have changed."""
        cell = _validate(name)
        if not isinstance(raw, str):
            raise TypeError("cell input must be a string")
        if raw.startswith("="):
            tree = parse_formula(raw[1:])
            # All mutations happen after this point; a bad formula leaves the
            # sheet untouched.
            precedents = references(tree)
            self._trees[cell] = tree
            self._raws[cell] = raw
            self._graph.set_dependencies(cell, precedents)
            self._values[cell] = None
        elif raw == "":
            self._graph.set_dependencies(cell, ())
            self._trees.pop(cell, None)
            self._raws.pop(cell, None)
            self._values.pop(cell, None)
        else:
            self._graph.set_dependencies(cell, ())
            self._trees.pop(cell, None)
            self._raws[cell] = raw
            stripped = raw.strip()
            if _NUMBER_RE.match(stripped):
                self._values[cell] = (
                    int(stripped) if "." not in stripped else float(stripped)
                )
            else:
                self._values[cell] = raw
        affected = self._graph.all_dependents(cell)
        affected.add(cell)
        ordered = sorted(affected, key=_sort_key)
        for target in ordered:
            if target in self._trees:
                if target in self._graph.cycle_cells():
                    self._values[target] = CYCLE
                else:
                    self._values[target] = evaluate(
                        self._trees[target], self._values.get
                    )
                    self.evaluations += 1
        return ordered

    def get(self, name):
        """Return the cell's value, or None for an empty cell."""
        return self._values.get(_validate(name))

    def raw(self, name: str) -> str:
        """Return the input last stored in the cell ('' when empty)."""
        return self._raws.get(_validate(name), "")

    def cells(self):
        """Return the non-empty cells in row-major order."""
        return sorted(self._raws, key=_sort_key)

            if text[0].isdigit():

            else:
                tokens.append(("ref", text))
        else:

        self.pos = 0

    def peek(self):

            return self.tokens[self.pos]
        return None

    def next(self):
        token = self.peek()
        if token is None:
            raise FormulaError("unexpected end of formula")
        self.pos += 1
        return token

    def parse(self):
        node = self.expr()
        if self.pos != len(self.tokens):
            raise FormulaError("unexpected trailing input")
        return node

    def expr(self):
        node = self.term()
        while True:
            token = self.peek()
            if token is not None and token[0] == "op" and token[1] in "+-":
                self.next()
                node = Binary(token[1], node, self.term())
            else:
                return node

    def term(self):
        node = self.unary()
        while True:
            token = self.peek()
            if token is not None and token[0] == "op" and token[1] in "*/":
                self.next()
                node = Binary(token[1], node, self.unary())
            else:
                return node

    def unary(self):
        token = self.peek()
        if token is not None and token[0] == "op" and token[1] in "+-":
            self.next()
            return Unary(token[1], self.unary())
        return self.primary()

    def primary(self):
        kind, text = self.next()
        if kind == "num":
            if "." in text:
                return Number(float(text))
            return Number(int(text))
        if kind == "ref":
            return Ref(_validate_ref(text))
        if text == "(":
            node = self.expr()
            token = self.peek()
            if token is None or token[1] != ")":
                raise FormulaError("unbalanced parentheses")
            self.next()
            return node
        raise FormulaError("incomplete expression")

    letters, digits = match.group(1), match.group(2)

        elif isinstance(node, Unary):
            visit(node.operand)
        elif isinstance(node, Binary):
            visit(node.left)
            visit(node.right)

    visit(tree)
    return found

    if isinstance(tree, Number):
        return tree.value
    if isinstance(tree, Ref):
        value = lookup(tree.name)

    if isinstance(tree, Unary):

        if isinstance(operand, ErrorValue):
            return operand
        if isinstance(operand, str):

            return -operand
        return +operand

        right = evaluate(tree.right, lookup)
        if isinstance(left, ErrorValue):
            return left
        if isinstance(right, ErrorValue):
            return right
        if isinstance(left, str) or isinstance(right, str):
            return ERROR
        if tree.op == "+":
            return left + right
        if tree.op == "-":
            return left - right
        if tree.op == "*":
            return left * right
        if right == 0:
            return ERROR
        return left / right

            nodes |= deps

        def reach(start, target):
            stack = list(self._prec.get(start, ()))
            seen = set()
            while stack:
                node = stack.pop()
                if node == target:
                    return True
                if node not in seen:
                    seen.add(node)
                    stack.extend(self._prec.get(node, ()))
            return False

            self._graph.set_dependencies(cell, references(tree))

        graph = self._graph

                    done.add(t)
                    progressed = True

        return self._values.get(cell)

    def raw(self, name):
        cell = _validate(name)
        return self._raws.get(cell, "")

import json
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone


class ParseError(ValueError):
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Record:
    time: datetime
    client: str
    method: str
    path: str
    status: int
    size: int
    latency_ms: float | None


_CLF_RE = re.compile(
    r'^(\S+) (\S+) (\S+) \[([^\]]+)\] "([^"]*)" (\d+) (\S+)(?: (\S+))?$'
)

_MONTHS = {
    "Jan": 1, "Feb": 2, "Mar": 3, "Apr": 4, "May": 5, "Jun": 6,
    "Jul": 7, "Aug": 8, "Sep": 9, "Oct": 10, "Nov": 11, "Dec": 12,
}

_CLF_TIME_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(\d{2})/([A-Za-z]{3})/(\d{4}):(\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2}) ([+-]\d{4})$"
)


def normalize(time, client, method, path, status, size, latency_ms) -> Record:
    if not isinstance(time, datetime):
        raise ParseError("time must be a datetime")
    if time.tzinfo is None:
        raise ParseError("time must be timezone-aware")
    time = time.astimezone(timezone.utc)

    if not isinstance(client, str) or not client:
        raise ParseError("client must be a non-empty string")

    if not isinstance(method, str) or not method or not method.isascii() or not method.isalpha():
        raise ParseError("method must be non-empty ASCII letters")
    method = method.upper()

    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path.startswith("/"):
        raise ParseError("path must start with /")
    path = re.split(r"[?#]", path, maxsplit=1)[0]
    path = re.sub(r"/+", "/", path)

    if isinstance(status, bool):
        raise ParseError("status must be an int")
    if isinstance(status, str):
        if not status.isdigit():
            raise ParseError("status must be digits")
        status = int(status)
    elif not isinstance(status, int):
        raise ParseError("status must be an int")
    if not 100 <= status <= 599:
        raise ParseError("status must be 100..599")

    if size is None or size == "-":
        size = 0
    elif isinstance(size, str):
        if not size.isdigit():
            raise ParseError("size must be digits")
        size = int(size)
    elif isinstance(size, bool) or not isinstance(size, int):
        raise ParseError("size must be a non-negative int")
    if size < 0:
        raise ParseError("size must be non-negative")

    if latency_ms is None:
        latency = None
    elif isinstance(latency_ms, bool) or not isinstance(latency_ms, (int, float)):
        raise ParseError("latency_ms must be a number")
    else:
        latency = float(latency_ms)
        if latency < 0:
            raise ParseError("latency_ms must be non-negative")

    return Record(
        time=time,
        client=client,
        method=method,
        path=path,
        status=status,
        size=size,
        latency_ms=latency,
    )


def _parse_clf_time(s: str) -> datetime:
    m = _CLF_TIME_RE.match(s)
    if not m:
        raise ParseError(f"bad time format: {s}")
    day, mon, year, hh, mm, ss, off = m.groups()
    month = _MONTHS.get(mon.title())
    if month is None:
        raise ParseError(f"bad month: {mon}")
    sign = 1 if off[0] == "+" else -1
    oh, om = int(off[1:3]), int(off[3:5])
    tz = timezone(sign * timedelta(hours=oh, minutes=om))
    try:
        return datetime(int(year), month, int(day), int(hh), int(mm), int(ss), tzinfo=tz)
    except ValueError as e:
        raise ParseError(f"bad time: {e}")


def parse_clf(line: str) -> Record:
    m = _CLF_RE.match(line)
    if not m:
        raise ParseError("line does not match common log format")
    client, _ident, _user, time_str, request, status, size, extra = m.groups()

    if extra is not None and (not extra.isdigit()):
        raise ParseError(f"bad response time: {extra}")
    latency_ms = int(extra) / 1000.0 if extra is not None else None

    parts = request.split(" ")
    if len(parts) != 3:
        raise ParseError("request must have three parts")
    method, path, _proto = parts

    return normalize(
        _parse_clf_time(time_str), client, method, path, status, size, latency_ms
    )


def parse_jsonl(line: str) -> Record:
    try:
        obj = json.loads(line)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        raise ParseError(f"invalid JSON: {e}")
    if not isinstance(obj, dict):
        raise ParseError("JSON value is not an object")
    for key in ("ts", "client", "method", "path", "status"):
        if key not in obj:
            raise ParseError(f"missing key: {key}")

    ts = obj["ts"]
    if not isinstance(ts, str):
        raise ParseError("ts must be a string")
    s = ts
    if s.endswith("Z"):
        s = s[:-1] + "+00:00"
    try:
        time = datetime.fromisoformat(s)
    except ValueError as e:
        raise ParseError(f"bad ts: {e}")
    if time.tzinfo is None:
        raise ParseError("ts must include a UTC offset")

    return normalize(
        time,
        obj["client"],
        obj["method"],
        obj["path"],
        obj["status"],
        obj.get("bytes"),
        obj.get("latency_ms"),
    )


def parse_line(line: str, fmt: str = "auto") -> Record:
    if fmt == "auto":
        if line.lstrip().startswith("{"):
            return parse_jsonl(line)
        return parse_clf(line)
    if fmt == "clf":
        return parse_clf(line)
    if fmt == "jsonl":
        return parse_jsonl(line)
    raise ValueError(f"unknown format: {fmt}")


def read_records(lines, fmt: str = "auto") -> tuple[list[Record], list[int]]:
    records: list[Record] = []
    bad: list[int] = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        try:
            records.append(parse_line(line, fmt))
        except ParseError:
            bad.append(i)
    return records, bad

import math
import re
from collections import Counter


def percentile(values, p):
    if not values:
        raise ValueError("values must not be empty")
    if not 0 < p <= 100:
        raise ValueError("p must be in (0, 100]")
    ordered = sorted(values)
    rank = math.ceil(p / 100 * len(ordered))
    return ordered[rank - 1]


_STATUS_CLASS_RE = re.compile(r"^([1-5])xx$")
_STATUS_EXACT_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{3}$")


def _matches_status(record, spec: str) -> bool:
    m = _STATUS_CLASS_RE.match(spec)
    if m:
        lo = int(m.group(1)) * 100
        return lo <= record.status <= lo + 99
    if _STATUS_EXACT_RE.match(spec):
        return record.status == int(spec)
    raise ValueError(f"bad status filter: {spec}")


def filter_records(records, since=None, until=None, status=None):
    out = []
    for r in records:
        if since is not None and r.time < since:
            continue
        if until is not None and not r.time < until:
            continue
        if status is not None and not _matches_status(r, status):
            continue
        out.append(r)
    return out


def summarize(records, top: int = 3):
    if top < 0:
        raise ValueError("top must be >= 0")

    count = len(records)
    total_bytes = sum(r.size for r in records)

    classes = {f"{c}xx": 0 for c in range(1, 6)}
    codes: Counter = Counter()
    latencies: list[float] = []
    paths: Counter = Counter()

    times = []
    for r in records:
        cls = f"{r.status // 100}xx"
        classes[cls] += 1
        codes[str(r.status)] += 1
        if r.latency_ms is not None:
            latencies.append(r.latency_ms)
        paths[r.path] += 1
        times.append(r.time)

    latency_stats = {
        "count": len(latencies),
        "p50": percentile(latencies, 50) if latencies else None,
        "p95": percentile(latencies, 95) if latencies else None,
        "max": max(latencies) if latencies else None,
    }

    ordered_paths = sorted(paths.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))
    top_paths = [[path, n] for path, n in ordered_paths[:top]]

    first = min(times).isoformat() if times else None
    last = max(times).isoformat() if times else None

    return {
        "requests": count,
        "bytes": total_bytes,
        "classes": classes,
        "codes": dict(sorted(codes.items(), key=lambda kv: int(kv[0]))),
        "latency_ms": latency_stats,
        "top_paths": top_paths,
        "first": first,
        "last": last,
    }
